# Dockingbird

> Dockingbird runs Claude Code and Codex side by side on your git repo, each agent in its own container.

These are the customer docs, one line per page in reading order. Search them from a clone with `python3 search/search.py "your words"` ([how the search ranks](docs/search.md)). [docs/manifest.json](docs/manifest.json) lists the same pages with their audience, commands and message ids.

## Start here

- [Dockingbird](README.md): Dockingbird runs Claude Code and Codex side by side on your git repo, each agent in its own container.
- [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md): The one-page path from a fresh computer to a first agent, a daily loop and a clean uninstall.
- [Prerequisites](docs/getting-started/prerequisites.md): What a computer needs before Dockingbird installs, with one check for each item.
- [Install](docs/getting-started/install.md): Install the dockingbird command from Zeusfyi's release index with a license key, and check that it runs.
- [Activate](docs/getting-started/activate.md): Give this computer its seat with a license key, or start a trial, and read the result.
- [First run](docs/getting-started/first-run.md): Make a repository ready with init, start the first agent, sign it in, and learn what the product prints at each point.
- [Choose a topology](docs/getting-started/choose-a-topology.md): Pick one computer, two computers over ssh, a cloud VM or a team pool, and see which pages and examples each needs.
- [Agent set-up prompt](docs/agent-setup-prompt.md): A block of plain text to paste into Claude Code or Codex so that it sets up Dockingbird on this computer with you.
- [Frequently asked questions](docs/faq.md): Thirteen first-week questions, each answered in three lines with one link to the page that holds the detail.

## Concepts

- [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md): A host runs the dockingbird command and one or more homes, each home runs one container per agent, and the agents' commits come back over sync.
- [Glossary](docs/concepts/glossary.md): One short entry for each word the Dockingbird docs use for a part of the product, with a link to the page that explains it.
- [Agents and the bus](docs/concepts/agents-and-the-bus.md): How a task reaches an agent, how its answers come back, what each bus command moves, and what an agent's life looks like from start to stop.
- [The sync model](docs/concepts/sync-model.md): How the agents' commits reach your branch and yours reach them, what sync does when one or both sides moved, and what it refuses.
- [Claude Code and Codex](docs/concepts/claude-code-and-codex.md): Where the two tools an agent runs differ in Dockingbird, covering sign-in, naming, one-shot forms, API keys, config keys, rules files and versions.
- [Swarms and roles](docs/concepts/swarms-and-roles.md): What a swarm definition holds, how roles, counts and send_to shape a team, how values are given at submit, and what a workload is.
- [Fleet and hosts](docs/concepts/fleet-and-hosts.md): How the hosts file differs from the scheduler's pool, why a host keeps one name, how placement orders hosts, and what a worker and an admitter do.
- [The fleet scheduler](docs/concepts/fleet-scheduler.md): The fleet scheduler is a pool of hosts on your organisation's PostgreSQL store that queues swarms and check runs and admits each where it fits.
- [The control plane](docs/concepts/control-plane.md): The control plane is a home of its own that other computers join, so an agent on one computer can message an agent on another.
- [Licensing model](docs/concepts/licensing-model.md): What a seat and a computer are, what a check-in does, how a license behaves offline and at the end of its term, and that this release does not enforce it.
- [Hosting paradigms](docs/concepts/hosting-paradigms.md): The three ways to arrange the organisation's store and the hosts, who runs each part in each, and which one a customer can use today.
- [Security model](docs/concepts/security-model.md): What an agent can reach, what it cannot, where secrets live, how the four egress modes limit its network, and what clean --all removes.
- [Observability](docs/concepts/observability.md): Dockingbird gives numbers from three sources, each agent, each host and the fleet scheduler's admitter, and never any message text or repository content.

## Guides

- [The daily loop](docs/guides/daily-loop.md): Start an agent at your terminal, read status, take its commits with sync, stop, and recover when a laptop sleeps, a terminal closes or an agent ends with work not shared.
- [Delegating tasks](docs/guides/delegating-tasks.md): Hand an agent a task on the bus, wait for it, read its messages, answer its questions, send more work and save its files.
- [Connections](docs/guides/connections.md): A connection lets agents use a GitHub repo, a folder, a database, a program, an MCP server or a browser while the secret stays with Dockingbird.
- [Your own commands](docs/guides/your-own-commands.md): Add a command of your own, such as dockingbird review, from a TOML config in your repo or one shared by every repo.
- [Give agents skills](docs/guides/skills.md): Give an agent skills its tool lists as its own, at one start, from a config, on a running agent or for a swarm role.
- [Toolchains and dependencies](docs/guides/toolchains.md): See, install, lock and change the language versions agents get from your repo's mise.toml or .tool-versions.
- [Trust and repo settings](docs/guides/trust-and-repo-settings.md): Decide which checkouts load their own settings, hooks, MCP servers, rules and dependency installs inside an agent, and add rules of your own for every agent.
- [Sign-in and API keys](docs/guides/sign-in-and-api-keys.md): Reuse the Claude and Codex logins already on your computer, sign in again or as someone else, use an API key, and sign out.
- [Egress and what agents can reach](docs/guides/egress-and-network.md): Choose how far an agent reaches on the network, with four egress modes, an allowlist, and what a blocked host sees.
- [Hosts](docs/guides/hosts.md): Add a second computer or a cloud VM as a host, read every agent on every host, attach to one, and read one Mac's load.
- [Licensing](docs/guides/licensing.md): Activate a computer, read its status, list and free seats, move a seat to a new laptop, give a seat back, start a trial, and read each license message.
- [Updates](docs/guides/updates.md): Check for a new release, update with or without agents running, pin a tool version, read homes on other versions, and move a fleet to a release.
- [Start agents from your own Claude Code or Codex](docs/guides/mcp-server.md): Install dockingbird mcp into your own harness so it starts agents, messages them, reads their replies and saves their results through eleven tools.
- [Clean and uninstall](docs/guides/clean-and-uninstall.md): Free disk, delete stopped agents, remove everything Dockingbird made, give the seat back and uninstall the tool.
- [Backup and restore](docs/guides/backup-and-restore.md): What a Dockingbird home and its Docker volumes hold, what to save before you replace a computer, and how to start fresh on the new one.
- [Data and privacy](docs/guides/data-and-privacy.md): What leaves your computer when you use Dockingbird, where its data is kept, and the commands that show it.
- [Networking](docs/guides/networking.md): The three network routes Dockingbird uses, what each needs reachable, what nothing else needs, and a check with a done line for each.
- [Tailscale](docs/guides/tailscale.md): Use a tailnet as the fleet's network, with the hub address, the serve line, the grant for a tagged VM and MagicDNS names for ssh.
- [Other networks](docs/guides/other-networks.md): Reach hosts over a bastion with ProxyJump, a WireGuard mesh or a gcloud VM with no public IP, and write each into hosts.toml.
- [Cloud VMs](docs/guides/cloud-vms.md): Prepare a Linux VM as a host, add it through gcloud or ssh, let the pool's admitter start it when stopped, size its disk, and join it to a fleet.
- [Connect agents to GitHub](docs/guides/github.md): Connect one GitHub branch so agents fetch and push it while the ssh key stays with Dockingbird.
- [MCP servers, services and browsers for agents](docs/guides/mcp-and-services.md): Give agents an MCP server by URL, a program of yours with typed arguments, or a browser, and serve them as yourself.
- [Give agents a database](docs/guides/databases.md): Connect a PostgreSQL database so agents query it, and write to it through a broker, without ever seeing its address or password.
- [Sign agents in with a password vault](docs/guides/secrets-vault.md): Connect a gopass store so Dockingbird types a login's password and one-time code into an agent's browser, and the agent sees neither.
- [Swarms](docs/guides/swarms.md): Write a swarm definition, check it, submit it with values, follow it in the queue and change it while it runs.
- [The work queue](docs/guides/work-queue.md): Keep one board of items, agents and requests in the organisation's store that people, scripts and agents read and write from any computer.
- [Install a team fleet](docs/guides/team-fleet.md): Install the PostgreSQL store, the roles, the worker and admitter services and the control plane that let a team share hosts and message across computers.
- [Run work on the fleet pool](docs/guides/fleet-scheduler.md): Enrol hosts in the pool, read the queue, see why a workload waits, control it, run a check under a lease and move the pool to a release.
- [Read the metrics by hand](docs/guides/metrics.md): Read the figures of a host, a home, its agents and the fleet scheduler with five commands, before you set up any collector.
- [Collect the metrics with Prometheus](docs/guides/prometheus.md): Run the example exporter on each host and point a Prometheus at it, and at the fleet scheduler's admitter, with two scrape jobs.
- [Draw the metrics in Grafana](docs/guides/grafana.md): Import the default Dockingbird dashboard into your own Grafana, read its five rows, add a host, and set three alerts.
- [Harbor benchmark tasks](docs/guides/harbor.md): Run a Harbor benchmark task's two baselines and one real trial with your own login, then list, read and clean its jobs.
- [The GUI](docs/guides/gui.md): What the Dockingbird GUI is, that its install is not yet available to customers, and what dockingbird ui prints today.

## Cookbooks and examples

- [One Mac, day one](examples/one-mac/README.md): Install, activate, start a first agent, hand a second one a task and take their commits with sync, on one Apple silicon Mac.
- [Recover from a failed install](examples/recover-from-a-failed-install/README.md): Check the platform, remove a bare install, install with the key, and fix the three failures: no index, a wrong key and a wrong platform.
- [Move your seat to a new laptop](examples/move-your-seat/README.md): Free the old computer's link, activate the new one, and read what status shows on each.
- [Give agents a database without the password](examples/database-without-the-password/README.md): Connect a PostgreSQL database for reads and brokered writes, add a service file with typed arguments, grant it to a swarm role, and revoke it.
- [Your own review command](examples/your-own-review-command/README.md): Write a .dockingbird/review.toml with a skill and instructions, run dockingbird review in the repo, then register it for every repo.
- [Two Macs over ssh](examples/two-macs-ssh/README.md): Add a second Mac as a host over ssh, fix its PATH and Docker socket, read its agents and attach to one.
- [A Mac and a cloud VM over gcloud](examples/cloud-vm-gcloud/README.md): Add a Compute Engine VM as a host through gcloud and read its agents.
- [Lock the tools your agents run](examples/lock-tool-versions/README.md): Pin Claude Code or Codex to one version, check what runs, and follow the latest release again.
- [Restrict what agents can reach](examples/restrict-egress/README.md): Limit new agents to their tool's hosts, the package registries and two hosts of your own, and see what a blocked request looks like.
- [Update with agents running](examples/update-with-agents-running/README.md): Update Dockingbird while agents work, watch each agent switch at its next stopping point, and finish the stragglers.
- [Before you replace a computer](examples/before-you-replace-a-computer/README.md): Save results, configs and hosts.toml, give the seat back, and start fresh on the new computer.
- [A team fleet on PostgreSQL](examples/team-fleet/README.md): Share a pool of two hosts through an organisation store, log in with org login, run a worker on each host and the admitter on one, queue a swarm and update the pool.
- [A swarm from a role library](examples/swarm-from-a-role-library/README.md): Submit a coordinator and four graders built from library roles, with helpers, values at submit and scores written through the broker.
- [Join a second computer to a control plane](examples/join-a-computer-to-a-control-plane/README.md): Make a control plane, join a second computer with its own bundle, read its status, remove it, and join it again after a lost home.
- [Uninstall completely](examples/uninstall-completely/README.md): Stop every agent, clean everything Dockingbird made, give the seat back, remove the tool and prune Docker's build cache.
- [A fleet on a tailnet](examples/fleet-on-a-tailnet/README.md): Make one home the control plane at its tailnet address, serve its hub port, grant a tagged VM access, and join each computer once.
- [A host behind a bastion](examples/host-behind-a-bastion/README.md): Reach a host that only a bastion reaches with a ProxyJump entry, add it with fleet hosts set, and fix its PATH.
- [Prometheus and Grafana for a fleet](examples/observability/README.md): Run the exporter on each host, add two scrape jobs to Prometheus, import the default dashboard into Grafana and set one alert.
- [Run a test suite under a lease](examples/test-suite-under-a-lease/README.md): Reserve cores and memory on the fleet pool for one command, wait for a host to take the lease, and run the command with the lease's size in its environment.
- [Change a running swarm](examples/change-a-running-swarm/README.md): Add two agents of a role to a running swarm, retire one, and prune the agents' copies after the branch is merged.

## Templates

- [Rules for the agents in this repository](templates/AGENTS.md): A template AGENTS.md for your own repository, which every agent Dockingbird runs there reads after Dockingbird's own rules.

## Troubleshooting

- [Install fails](docs/troubleshooting/install-fails.md): Each way the install can stop, in the order you meet it, with what the screen shows and the fix.
- [License refused](docs/troubleshooting/licence-refused.md): Each way a license command or a license check can stop you, in the order you meet it, with what the screen shows and the fix.
- [First start stops](docs/troubleshooting/first-start-stops.md): Each place the first dockingbird claude can stop, in the order you meet it, with what the screen shows and the fix.
- [Troubleshooting index: install, Docker, licensing and the command line](docs/troubleshooting/install.md): The 63 message ids about installing, Docker, the license and typing a command, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: homes, checkouts and toolchains](docs/troubleshooting/homes.md): The 113 message ids about Dockingbird homes, your checkout and its branches, init, toolchains, project rules and trust, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: agents, status, sync and clean](docs/troubleshooting/agents.md): The 325 message ids about starting agents, their status, sync, stop and clean, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: the bus](docs/troubleshooting/bus.md): The 72 message ids about tasks on the bus: send, wait, the inbox, read, questions and results, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: configs, connections and host resources](docs/troubleshooting/connections.md): The 204 message ids about your own commands, connections, served resources, browsers and watch, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: the fleet, swarms and the work queue](docs/troubleshooting/fleet.md): The 222 message ids about hosts, the fleet scheduler, the control plane, swarms and the work queue, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: benchmark jobs](docs/troubleshooting/benchmarks.md): The 51 message ids about Harbor benchmark jobs, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: sign-ins and the org store](docs/troubleshooting/sign-ins.md): The 91 message ids about signing in, API keys, signing out and the org login, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: updates](docs/troubleshooting/updates.md): The 49 message ids about checking for and installing updates, pins and the switch to a new version, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting index: the GUI, the MCP server and shell completion](docs/troubleshooting/gui-and-mcp.md): The 27 message ids about the GUI, the MCP server and shell completion, each with when it appears.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): Every message Dockingbird prints, by id: when it appears, its text, the next step it gives and its exit status.

## Reference

- [Commands](docs/reference/commands.md): Every command a customer can type, with its arguments, one line of purpose, its exit statuses and the guide that explains it.
- [Exit codes](docs/reference/integration/exit-codes.md): The one table of the exit statuses a dockingbird command ends with, and what a script does on each.
- [The --json envelope](docs/reference/integration/json.md): The keys of the one-line JSON envelope every message becomes under --json, and how a script reads it.
- [The dockingbird mcp host tools](docs/reference/integration/mcp.md): The eleven tools the dockingbird mcp server gives your own Claude Code or Codex, with each tool's arguments.
- [Compatibility, what you can build on](docs/reference/integration/compatibility.md): The surfaces a script may rely on and the promise about how they change between releases.
- [hosts.toml](docs/reference/files/hosts-file.md): Every key of hosts.toml, the file that names the other computers you reach, and the commands that write it.
- [org.toml and the password file](docs/reference/files/org-file.md): The keys of org.toml, the file that names your organisation's store, and the ~/.pgpass line that holds each role's password.
- [Swarm definition file](docs/reference/files/swarm-definition.md): Every top-level key and every role key of a swarm definition at schema 1, with its type, default and meaning.
- [app.toml, the keys of a config](docs/reference/files/app-config.md): Every key of a config file such as .dockingbird/app.toml, with its values, its default and what it fixes.
- [Role and connection files](docs/reference/files/roles-and-connections.md): The keys of a library role file, a service connection file with its argument keys, and a subagent block.
- [What dockingbird init writes](docs/reference/files/project-file.md): The files dockingbird init writes into a repo, and every key of .dockingbird/project.toml.
- [The home folder layout](docs/reference/files/home-layout.md): What lives where under a Dockingbird home, which files you may edit, and how a second home by name works.
- [The fleet store](docs/reference/files/fleet-store.md): The three schemas of the organisation's PostgreSQL 18 store, its role groups, the order of a migration and which migrations need older workers restarted first.
- [Environment variables](docs/reference/environment-variables.md): The DOCKINGBIRD_ variables you may set, how Dockingbird treats a setting, and the variables of other tools it reads.
- [Limits](docs/reference/limits.md): The bounds on sessions, files, names, licenses and fleet calls that the Dockingbird guide states, one row each with its figure.
- [Ports and hosts](docs/reference/ports-and-hosts.md): Every port and route Dockingbird opens or expects, on which interface, with the timeouts of each and the hosts an egress preset reaches.
- [Metrics reference](docs/reference/metrics.md): Every metric family Dockingbird serves, with its type, labels and unit, the agent families first, the fleet families second and the exporter's own gauges last.
- [Fleet tools](docs/reference/fleet-tools.md): The ten fleet tools an agent on a joined home gets beside its bus tools, with who each can reach.
- [Search the docs](docs/search.md): Search these docs from a clone with one Python command, offline, and see how it ranks what it finds.

- [Operator guide](docs/operator-guide.md): The long form of the Dockingbird docs, one section per topic, from install and sync to the fleet, configs, files and egress.
